source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio SAT5-SAT6 campus publishes 33 MW of IT capacity across 175,000 square feet, sixth among Texas data centers that disclose power and 6.9% of the state's 475 MW published total.

The same 33 MW translates into very different amounts of compute depending on rack density. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training figure, it supports roughly 825 racks. At 100 kW per rack for GPU-dense inference, roughly 330. Power is the fixed input and rack count is the variable, so a megawatt figure alone does not fix how much hardware sits inside a building.

The certifications, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, TIA-942 and HITRUST, qualify the campus for regulated workloads in payment, health and federal systems. That points to an enterprise and government tenancy profile rather than an AI-specific one. The data does not say which workloads actually run there, and the suitability score of 68 is built only from published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities and only 19 publish power capacity. Every ranking above is therefore a ranking among the disclosing minority, and the state's real IT load is unknown. The record also carries no address, no coordinates and no nearest airport, so nothing here speaks to substation proximity, interconnection queue position or on-site generation, which are the details that decide whether 33 MW can actually be delivered.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
